body_html:
Knowing how to compliment food in Spanish is one of the quickest ways to win hearts, especially at your partner’s family table. In Spanish-speaking cultures, food is love, and praising the cook is expected, appreciated and often reciprocated with another huge plate. Delicioso is correct, but natives use a whole range of warmer, more colorful expressions. Here are the ones you’ll actually hear, from everyday ¡Qué rico! to the enthusiastic ¡Está para chuparse los dedos!

Key takeaways
  • ¡Qué rico! and ¡Está buenísimo! are the most natural compliments.
  • Use estar for how food tastes: La sopa está riquísima.
  • Praise the cook directly: ¡Cocinas de maravilla!
  • Asking for the recipe is the highest compliment: ¿Me das la receta?
{{toc}}

How to compliment food in Spanish: the essentials

SpanishEnglishNotes
¡Qué rico!How tasty!Everywhere, very common
¡Está buenísimo!It’s really good!Everywhere
¡Está riquísimo!It’s delicious!Warm and natural
¡Qué delicioso!How delicious!A bit more formal
¡Está de muerte!It’s to die for!Spain, informal
¡Está para chuparse los dedos!It’s finger-licking good!Everywhere, enthusiastic

The RAE dictionary lists “tasty, pleasant to the taste” among the meanings of rico, which is why it works so well for food.

Use estar for taste

When you describe how food tastes right now, use estar: El pollo está buenísimo. Using ser describes the dish in general: La paella es un plato típico de Valencia. Remember: estar bueno about a person means something else entirely! See {{link:bueno-vs-bien|bueno vs bien}} and {{link:ser-vs-estar|ser vs estar}}.

Describing specific qualities

  • Está en su punto. It’s cooked perfectly.
  • La carne está muy tierna. The meat is very tender.
  • Tiene un sabor increíble. It has an amazing flavor.
  • Está muy jugoso. It’s very juicy.
  • La salsa está espectacular. The sauce is spectacular.
  • El postre está de diez. The dessert is perfect (a 10/10).
{{image:2}}

Praising the cook

  • ¡Cocinas de maravilla! You cook wonderfully!
  • Tienes muy buena mano para la cocina. You have a real gift for cooking.
  • Son los mejores tamales que he probado. These are the best tamales I’ve ever tasted.
  • Se nota que lo has hecho con cariño. You can tell it was made with love.
  • ¡Qué buena cocinera es tu madre! Your mom is such a good cook!

Saying this to your partner’s parents is a classic way to start well; see {{link:meeting-your-partners-family-in-spanish|meeting your partner’s family in Spanish}}.

Asking for more and for the recipe

  • ¿Me das un poquito más? Could I have a little more?
  • No puedo resistirme, voy a repetir. I can’t resist, I’ll have seconds.
  • ¿Me das la receta? Will you give me the recipe?
  • ¿Cómo lo haces? ¿Cuál es el secreto? How do you make it? What’s the secret?
{{book:a-road-in-bloom}}

Saying you’re full, politely

Hosts often insist. To decline without offending:

  • Estoy lleno/a, de verdad. Estaba todo buenísimo. I’m full, really. Everything was delicious.
  • No puedo más, pero me encantó. I can’t eat any more, but I loved it.
  • Bueno, solo un poquito. Well, just a little. (often the best answer!)

At a restaurant

To compliment food when eating out: Todo estaba buenísimo, felicite al cocinero (Everything was delicious, my compliments to the chef), or simply ¡Muy rico todo, gracias! when the waiter clears the plates. For ordering, see {{link:ordering-food-in-spanish|ordering food in Spanish}}.

A sample conversation

  • Suegra: ¿Qué tal el cocido? (How’s the stew?)
  • You: ¡Está riquísimo! La carne está tiernísima. (It’s delicious! The meat is so tender.)
  • Suegra: Ay, gracias. ¿Quieres más? (Oh, thank you. Do you want more?)
  • You: Bueno, un poquito más. ¿Me darás la receta algún día? (Well, a little more. Will you give me the recipe one day?)

Cultural notes

Across Spain and Latin America, complimenting food is part of good manners, not flattery. A silent meal can make the cook wonder whether you liked it. Say ¡Buen provecho! when people start eating, compliment early, and stay at the table afterward for the sobremesa, the relaxed conversation that follows a meal. Finishing your plate is usually appreciated, though in some places leaving a tiny bit signals that you were given plenty. More etiquette in {{link:family-dinner-spanish-phrases|family dinner Spanish phrases}}.

Regional favorites

Every country has its own way to say something is delicious. In Mexico you’ll hear ¡Está buenísimo! and ¡Qué sabroso!; in Colombia and Venezuela, ¡Qué sabroso! is everywhere; in Argentina, ¡Está buenísimo! or ¡Qué rico!; in Spain, informal favorites include ¡Está de vicio! and ¡Está de muerte!. In Chile, people say ¡Está exquisito! or ¡Qué rico!. If you’re unsure, ¡Qué rico! works in every Spanish-speaking country and never sounds wrong.

Thanking the host after the meal

When the meal ends, a final thank-you goes a long way: Muchas gracias por la comida, estaba todo buenísimo (Thank you so much for the meal, everything was delicious), Me he puesto las botas (I’ve eaten like a king, Spain), or La próxima vez cocino yo (Next time I’ll cook). If you were invited to someone’s home, a message the next day saying Gracias otra vez por la cena de anoche is a lovely touch.

Common mistakes

MistakeBetterWhy
Es delicioso. (about this plate)Está delicioso.Current taste: estar
La comida está caliente (meaning spicy)La comida pica / está picante.Caliente = hot temperature
Estoy completo.Estoy lleno.Literal translation
Muy bueno comida.La comida está muy buena.Gender agreement

Final thoughts

Start with ¡Qué rico!, add a specific detail, praise the cook and ask for the recipe. You’ll make friends at every table. For more everyday situations, see {{link:spanish-phrases-for-everyday-situations|my guide to Spanish phrases for everyday situations}}.

faq.q: How do you say “this is delicious” in Spanish?
How do you compliment someone’s cooking in Spanish?
faq.a: ¡Cocinas de maravilla!, Tienes muy buena mano para la cocina or Es la mejor tortilla que he probado.

faq.q: How do you say “I’m full” in Spanish?
faq.a: Estoy lleno (male) or Estoy llena (female). You can add: Estaba todo buenísimo.
